title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a working note on the divided-power de Rham complex. It is a typescript page, numbered '-155-' with running head 'IX', from Grothendieck's SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §12 on Jacobians of semistable curves. It has been interleaved in the archive folder.

Setting. C is a reduced curve with ordinary double points over an algebraically closed field.
- J is the set of irreducible components, with normalizations C̃_j.
- I is the set of singular points.
- K is the set of branches, i.e. points of the normalization lying over I.
- h: K → I×J sends a branch to its singular point and its component.
- The page opens at the end of a sentence describing a group (probably the character group of the torus part of Pic^0_C, from (12.3.6)) as the cokernel of Z^{I×J} → Z^K induced by h, transposed of Z^{(h)}.

Dual graph. The dual graph Γ(C) has vertices Γ_0 = J. Its edges are Γ_1 = (K ×_I K − Δ(K))/symmetry: one edge for each pair of distinct branches through the same singular point. After choosing orientations, an edge is written (x, C', C''). Then
- H_1(Γ(C),Z) = Ker(d: Z^{(Γ_1)} → Z^{(J)}), with d(x,C',C'') = g(C'') − g(C') (12.3.11–12).
- The comparison map (12.3.8) is induced by a morphism of two-term chain complexes v = (v_0, v_1): [Z^{(Γ_1)} → Z^{(J)}] → [Z^{(K)} → Z^{(I×J)}].
- It is given by v_1(x,C',C'') = (x,C'') − (x,C') and v_0(C̃_j) = (0, C̃_j) (12.3.13–14).

12.4. Here X is a semistable curve over a strictly henselian trait with special fibre X_0. Combining (12.1.12) with (12.3.6) for C = X_0 gives the classical result. The character group M of the maximal torus T_0 of the special fibre of the Néron model of A = Pic^0_{X_η/η} is M = Ker(Z^I → Z^J) = H_1(dual graph of X_0, Z), the boundary map being defined via the oriented edges. This is the input for Grothendieck's monodromy pairing and component-group computations in SGA 7 IX §12.
errors: In (12.3.13) the source term is written Z^{(Γ)}; from (12.3.11) it should be Z^{(Γ_1)}.
The notation in (12.3.14) for v_0, '(0, C̃_j)', is somewhat opaque out of context; it presumably depends on conventions fixed on the preceding typescript page, which is not provided here.
Not mathematical: this page belongs to the SGA 7 typescript, not to the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes in which it is filed.

ideas.what: Character group of the toric part of the special fibre of the Néron model of a Jacobian of a semistable curve equals H_1 of the dual graph of the special fibre
ideas.modern_name: Toric rank / character group via the dual graph (Raynaud–Grothendieck)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Raynaud (1970, Spécialisation du foncteur de Picard) and Grothendieck (SGA 7 IX §12)

ideas.what: Explicit description of the dual graph and its cellular chain complex from branch data h: K → I×J, with a comparison morphism of two-term complexes
ideas.modern_name: Dual graph of a nodal curve; cellular homology

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX typescript (§12.3–12.4, page 155). Its content is the standard, well-credited dual-graph description of the torus part of Néron models of Jacobians. It is merely misfiled among the 1976 notes.
transcription_corrections: In (12.3.13), 'Z^{(Γ)}' should read 'Z^{(Γ_1)}' if that is the intended meaning; the typescript itself appears to show Γ without the subscript.
'arrêtes' appears as typed in the original; correct French is 'arêtes'.
